text:
Marathon Petroleum stock recovered 2.9% today after dropping sharply over the prior three days, when crude oil prices spiked on Middle East tensions—Brent crude hit $116 on October 23rd amid escalating Iran rhetoric and Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Today's bounce coincides with news that Saudi Arabia and Iran are now de-escalating through direct talks, which has eased the immediate supply-shock premium in oil prices (crude fell from the $116 peak). Refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with ample crude available, putting the company in position to benefit if geopolitical risk stays manageable while oil prices remain elevated.

The stock's whipsaw over the past week—up sharply early, then down hard when tensions peaked, now recovering—reflects how refiner profits depend heavily on oil price stability and predictability, not just the level of prices themselves. The recent geopolitical cycle has created that volatility, but the company's own operations appear intact and well-supplied.
